The verdict follows both starting lineups and the 2026 title odds, so it must read WIN FOR B (the partner), with one title-odds row for the current season whose Side A change is negative and whose before-to-after odds fall. Redraft renders no Year-by-Year block and no pick-derived rows, and a depth-or-better player carries nonzero value (McCaffrey's pile total is above 0). The sleep covers the 7,500-simulation run, about 10 seconds on this machine, which blocks the page. The button is clicked from an eval, not a harness click: the simulation holds the page as soon as the handler returns, and a harness click waits on the page for its own acknowledgement, so on a loaded machine (16 seconds, 2026-09-25) the click itself timed out at 15 seconds before the sleep could cover the run.

features.name: Stats Lab split engine: combined seasons, week range and a situation filter recompute the rows

path.eval: window.__cap = () => { const t = document.querySelector('table.stats-lab-table'); const hs = [...t.tHead.rows[0].cells].map(c => c.textContent.replace(/[\u2191\u2193]/g, '').trim()); const i = hs.indexOf('Tgt'), m = {}; for (const r of t.tBodies[0].rows) m[r.dataset.key] = Number(r.cells[i].textContent); return { split: t.dataset.split || '', m }; }; window.__pick = (sel, v) => { const s = document.querySelector(sel); s.value = v; s.dispatchEvent(new Event('change', { bubbles: true })); }; true;

features.assert: (() => { try { const A = window.ADVANCED, B = window.ADVANCED_BY_SEASON || {}, cur = A && A.season; if (!A || !B[cur - 1] || !B[cur - 2]) return false; const tgt = (P) => Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(P.players).map(([k, v]) => [k, v.targets || 0])); const a0 = tgt(A), a1 = tgt(B[cur - 1]), a2 = tgt(B[cur - 2]); const all = window.__all, std = window.__std, wk = window.__wk12, d3 = window.__d3; if (!all || !std || !wk || !d3) return false; const ids = (x) => Object.keys(x.m); /* three seasons = the three advanced.js files added up, row for row */ if (all.split !== `${cur - 2}+${cur - 1}+${cur}` || ids(all).length < 30) return false; if (!ids(all).every(k => all.m[k] === (a0[k] || 0) + (a1[k] || 0) + (a2[k] || 0))) return false; /* weeks 1 to the latest is season to date exactly; weeks 1-2 is never more and, past week 2, less for somebody */ if (ids(std).length < 30 || !ids(std).every(k => std.m[k] === (a0[k] || 0))) return false; if (!/weeks 1-2/.test(wk.split) || !ids(wk).every(k => wk.m[k] <= (a0[k] || 0))) return false; if (A.throughWeek > 2 && !ids(wk).some(k => wk.m[k] < (a0[k] || 0))) return false; /* a situation filter changes row values: 3rd down is never more than all downs, and less for somebody */ if (!/3rd down/.test(d3.split) || ids(d3).length < 10) return false; return ids(d3).every(k => k in wk.m && d3.m[k] <= wk.m[k]) && ids(d3).some(k => d3.m[k] < wk.m[k]); } finally { localStorage.removeItem('ff-stats-lab-v1'); } })()
features.notes: Data Suite gap cluster B. projections/build_split_cube.py writes site/data/splits-YYYY.js: counting stats per player x week x situation bucket (down, distance, field zone, score, play action, motion, QB spot, blitz, box), lazy-loaded like advanced-YYYY.js. The split card sums the picked seasons, weeks and buckets and recomputes the rates; one season with nothing else picked is still advanced.js. The path walks the season toggles (loading both past advanced files on the way), then weeks and a 3rd-down filter. The assert requires the three-season table to equal the three advanced.js files added per player, weeks 1 to the latest to equal season to date, weeks 1-2 to be smaller for someone, and 3rd down to be smaller still, so a split that re-reads the season totals or ignores a filter fails. Rows are keyed by Sleeper id (tr data-key) and the season buttons by position, so it survives a new season. It clears the Stats Lab prefs when done so later features start on the default view.

features.name: Stats Lab Coverage tab: man and zone splits match the payload, team shells render, 2026 says not published

path.eval: window.__covCap = () => { const t = document.querySelector('table.stats-lab-table'); const hs = [...t.tHead.rows[0].cells].map(c => c.textContent.replace(/[↑↓]/g, '').trim()); const i = hs.indexOf('Tgt'); return { rows: t.tBodies[0].rows.length, heads: hs, topTgt: i < 0 ? null : Number(t.tBodies[0].rows[0].cells[i].textContent) }; }; window.__covPick = (label, v) => { const s = document.querySelector("#main .stats-lab-filters select[aria-label='" + label + "']"); s.value = v; s.dispatchEvent(new Event('change', { bubbles: true })); }; true;

features.assert: (() => { const C = window.COVERAGE_BY_SEASON || {}, cur = window.ADVANCED.season, P = C[cur - 1]; if (!P || !P.published || !C[cur] || C[cur].published !== false) return false; const m = window.__covMan, z = window.__covZone, go = window.__covGo; if (!m || !z || !go || m.rows < 40 || z.rows < 40 || go.rows < 20 || !m.heads.includes('Tgt/DB') || !m.heads.includes('+/- all')) return false; /* default sort is targets, so the top row is the most-targeted WR in that split in the payload */ const wrs = Object.entries(P.players).filter(([, v]) => v.p === 'WR' && v.R); const top = (k) => Math.max(...wrs.map(([, v]) => v.R[k] ? v.R[k][1] : 0)); if (m.topTgt !== top(P.splits.indexOf('man')) || z.topTgt !== top(P.splits.indexOf('zone'))) return false; if (go.topTgt !== Math.max(...wrs.map(([s]) => ((P.targetedRoutes[s] || {}).GO || [0])[0]))) return false; if (P.league.tgt.man + P.league.tgt.zone > P.league.tgt.all || window.__covTeams !== 32) return false; const e = document.querySelector('.stats-lab-cov-empty'); return /not published yet/.test(e.textContent) && !!e.querySelector('button') && !document.querySelector('table.stats-lab-table') && document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= innerWidth + 1; })()
features.notes: Data Suite gap cluster C. projections/build_coverage_splits.py joins nflverse pbp_participation to play-by-play and writes site/data/coverage-YYYY.js (counts only, lazy-loaded): per receiver and QB vs man, vs zone, by shell (Cover 0, 1, 2, 2-man, 3, 4, 6), pressured and clean; per team personnel, formation and shells played and faced; per receiver the TARGETED route tree. With no season picked the tab shows the newest season nflverse has posted, so it opens on the prior season while 2026 participation 404s. The assert requires the man and zone top rows to equal the largest per-WR count in the payload, the targeted Go split to do the same from targetedRoutes, all 32 teams in the shell view, and picking the current season to render the not-published card (no table, a Show button, no sideways scroll). --self-check on the builder reconciles man plus zone targets with the participation file.

features.name: Stats Lab Coverage tab fits a phone, and the Teams tab carries each defense's shell mix

path.eval: window.__covTeamRow = (() => { const t = document.querySelector('table.stats-lab-table'); const hs = [...t.tHead.rows[0].cells].map(c => c.textContent.replace(/[↑↓]/g, '').trim()); const i = hs.indexOf('Man%'), r = [...t.tBodies[0].rows].find(x => x.dataset.key === 'DEN'); return r && { man: r.cells[i].textContent, zone: r.cells[hs.indexOf('Zone%')].textContent }; })(); location.hash='#stats/Coverage'

features.assert: (() => { const P = window.COVERAGE_BY_SEASON[window.ADVANCED.season - 1], v = P.teams.DEN.dcov, n = v[0] + v[1], got = window.__covTeamRow; if (!got || got.man !== (v[0] / n * 100).toFixed(1) + '%' || got.zone !== (v[1] / n * 100).toFixed(1) + '%') return false; const f = document.querySelector('#main .stats-lab-filters'), sels = [...f.querySelectorAll('select')]; if (sels.length !== 3) return false; const t = document.querySelector('table.stats-lab-table'), w = t.parentElement, name = t.querySelector('tbody tr td:nth-child(2)'); w.scrollLeft = w.scrollWidth; return document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= innerWidth + 1 && sels.every(s => { const r = s.getBoundingClientRect(); return r.width > 0 && r.left >= 0 && r.right <= innerWidth; }) && getComputedStyle(name).position === 'sticky' && w.scrollLeft > 0; })()
features.notes: At 390px the Coverage filters (position buttons, Season, Split, Min tgt) wrap inside the card with no sideways page scroll, and the table scrolls inside its own wrapper with the Player cell pinned, like every Stats Lab table. It first opens the Teams tab on the prior season: the Coverage (D) group adds Man%, Zone% and Cover 0-6 played from the same coverage-YYYY.js, fetched in the background the first time Teams asks, and Denver's Man% and Zone% must equal its dcov counts in the payload. On the current season Teams says the shell columns wait for nflverse participation instead of showing blanks.

ignoreReason: Draft Room calls the live Sleeper API on mount to list your 2026 drafts. That call is the one deliberately-online surface in an otherwise file:// app, so it fails in a headless offline run. Scoped to the single host: any other failed request still fails the gate.
